title: Set a restrictive page policy
summary: A Content Security Policy limits where a page can load and run content.
introduction: A Content Security Policy limits where a page can load and run content. Your task: Move any inline click script into renderer.js.
learningObjectives: Move any inline click script into renderer.js.
Explain the example for set a restrictive page policy

blocks.text: A Content Security Policy limits where a page can load and run content. For a local app, start with only local resources and external script files.

Use a local Electron project with electron installed as a dev dependency and main.cjs as its main file. Run with npx electron . after creating package.json and index.html. These APIs do not run in a web-page playground.

blocks.code:
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:">
<!-- Put this in index.html head; use local external JS and CSS files. -->
blocks.title: Set a restrictive page policy

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: self allows resources from this app's own origin.
The script rule omits unsafe-inline, so page behaviour needs an allowed external script file.

blocks.text: The page accepts the allowed local resources and blocks inline scripts under this policy.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not add unsafe-eval or unsafe-inline just to hide a setup error. Move code into appropriate files.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Move any inline click script into renderer.js.
